description: The Ushahidi Platform is a crowdsourcing and mapping tool that gathers reports from the public by web, SMS, email, social media and native mobile apps, lets teams review, verify and categorise them with custom surveys, and maps and analyses the results. Ushahidi, a non-profit technology company founded in Kenya, builds it so communities, responders and governments can turn citizen-generated data into action; it has been used after the Haiti and Nepal earthquakes, for COVID-19 response and for election monitoring. Coverage is global, with deployments in more than 160 countries and over 40 languages; each deployment defines its own area and period. Access is through hosted deployments created on the website, and the code is published as open source. Licence: open source, but the licence was not named on the pages read; the hosted service has free and paid tiers, so cost is recorded as freemium. Caveats: data quality depends on each deployment's moderation, and there is no central archive of reports. It supports emergency response and resilience work by collecting ground reports of damage and service outages. Related catalogue records are PetaBencana.id, a national crowdsourced disaster map, and the NYC 311 service requests.
